turns.note: First split C4- / C5+ to see cost scale.
Split C5-/C6+, then C4-/C5 and C6 paraffins / heavier to target C5 mix and C6 paraffin mix.
Target sharp nC5/22DMB split as the first cut (C5- top 1559 mol/s, C6+ bottoms).
Shift column 1 cut to C5-/C6+ by raising boil-up; then C4-/C5 mix and C6 paraffin mix/heavier.
Sharpen C5/C6 cut, sharpen C4/C5 cut to get C5 mix, and C6 paraffins vs naphthenes+heavy.
Shift cut points: more tops in feed column to get all C5 up, more tops in T column to strip C4 from the C5 mix, slightly less tops in B.
Push more nC5 overhead in feed column and sharpen C4/C5 split in T column to make C5 mix and C6 paraffin mix reach 95%.
Use empirical D/B vs rb/(1+R) calibration: sharpen feed column at ~1559 tops, T column raise tops to ~864 (all C4-), B column more stages/reflux to get C6 paraffin mix ≥95%.
Cut feed column tops to ~1565 to keep 22DMB out of C5 mix (TB at 94%); add C3-/C4 split on TT to sell C4 mix.
Split BB into C6 light/naphthenes tops vs C7+ and then heptane vs octane+nonane to sell pure heptane.
Sharpen BB cut (C6 naphthenes+hexane top ~360 vs C7+), split heptane, octane/nonane, and cyclohexane from hexane+MCP.

Heavy cuts are very valuable (heptane, octane, cyclohexane): retarget BB to send all heptane down, BBT to cut MCP/cyclohexane, BBB heptane/octane at D~205, BBBB octane/nonane; add deethanizer on TTT for C3 mix.
Make C3 mix sellable by stripping ethane harder in TTT; push heptane and octane toward 99% premium with more stages.
Push cyclohexane, heptane, octane to 99% premium by sharpening BB (less heptane in BBT), BBB and BBBB at the same cut points.
Turn 14 sharpening broke the cyclohexane and heptane cuts; going back to the turn-13 design to see its settings.
Push to premium grades by adding stages only (same reflux/boil-up keeps the cut points): BB for less heptane in cyclohexane, BBB for heptane, BBBB for octane.
Raise reflux while adjusting boil-up via vapour balance to keep the same distillate flows, aiming at 99% premium cyclohexane, heptane, octane.
Go back to the turn-13 best design to see its settings before trying smaller changes.
Use mass balance to cut heptane distillate to ~198 (all heptane, little octane) and octane distillate to ~233 (little nonane) to reach 99% premium.
Try to push cyclohexane to 99% premium by sharpening BB (more stages, same R/boil-up keeps the cut) so less heptane goes overhead.
Push all butane overhead in T (D~862) and split C5 mix into iC5 / nC5 (worth ~100-250M more than the blend).
T column failed; go back to the turn-19 best design to see its settings.
Root column costs $293M; lower reflux 3.5→2.6 with boil-up adjusted by vapour balance (same D) and add stages to keep C5/C6 cut sharp.
Sharpen T (more stages, same cut) to keep butane out of C5, then split C5 mix into isopentane/n-pentane (~+100M) at low pressure.
Turn-24 C5 split failed (butane leaks into isopentane); go back to the turn-23 best design.
Small polishing column on the 96% cyclohexane stream: strip the heptane into a small bottoms so the tops reach 99% premium (+~50M).
The cyclohexane polishing column lost value (98% not premium, and it took product away). Go back to the turn-23 best design.
Root column is the costliest; cut reflux 2.6→2.2 with boil-up set by vapour balance (same distillate) and add 10 stages to keep the C5/C6 cut sharp.
Turn-29 root reflux cut broke the C5/C6 cut; go back to the turn-23 best design.
BBTT (hexane+MCP, worthless) split: tops = C6 paraffin mix (nC6+3MP), bottoms = C6 naphthene mix (MCP+CH). Potential ~+200M.
Hexane/MCP split needs many stages and high reflux (alpha~1.1); try 200 stages R=20 with D~88 to get C6 paraffin tops and naphthene bottoms.
Drop worthless BBTT; sharpen T (60 stages, slightly more boil-up to push butane overhead) and split C5 mix into iC5/nC5 at low pressure with a tall column.
Back to the best design, and lower the reflux on the C7/C8 and C8/C9 columns, whose separations are easy (relative volatility about 2), with boil-up cut to match, to save energy.
Turn 34's lower reflux on the C7/C8 and C8/C9 columns lost purity. Go back to the best design so I can see its exact settings again.
More stages in BB to reduce heptane leaking into BBT so the cyclohexane bottoms of BBT reaches 99% premium (+~60M).
Sharpen nC4/iC5 cut in T (more stages, reflux, slightly larger distillate) and split C5 mix into iC5/nC5 at low pressure with high reflux; potential +100-250M.
Turn 37's T column failed to converge. Go back to the best valid design (5.132) and look at its exact settings again.
Try splitting the C5 mix alone (iC5 tops / nC5 bottoms) at low pressure; pure products worth ~+100-250M vs blend.
Back to the best design; sharpen the BBT column (more stages, slightly more reflux at the same split) to push cyclohexane bottoms from 96% to 99% premium (+~60M).
Heptane in cyclohexane bottoms comes from BB's CH/C7 cut; raise BB reflux (with matching boil-up) to cut heptane leak and reach premium cyclohexane.
Turn 41's higher BB reflux broke the downstream cuts. Going back to the best design (5.132) to see its settings before the next refinement.
Cut the cost of the feed column: lower the reflux and boil-up together so the split stays the same (C5/C6 cut is fairly easy).
Turn 43's cheaper feed column ruined the downstream split. Go back to the best design (5.132) to see its settings.
Split 2,2-dimethylbutane (lightest C6, alpha~1.3 vs 2MP) off the C6 paraffin blend as a pure tops; the bottoms should remain a C6 paraffin blend.
Revert to best, then split worthless BBTT (nC6/MCP) into a C6-paraffin-blend tops (~90 mol/s) and a C6-naphthene-blend bottoms (MCP+CH); ~200M potential vs ~90M cost.

Stopping with the best valid design from turn 23 (reward 5.132). Recent changes to the feed, BB, the C5 split, the 2,2-dimethylbutane split and the nC6/MCP split all scored lower or failed. The rest of the possible gains are small and would cost more in columns than they bring in.
